newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-With blue chips in vogue, few stars seen.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-With blue chips in vogue, few stars seen.

text.p: Wall Street's latest craze for blue chip stocks has left the market for initial public offerings largely out in the cold with only high quality companies able to drum up enough hype for opening premiums.
Few of this week's deals are expected to shine when they debut on the stock market, analysts say.
"This is uncharacteristic for the fourth quarter, there's usually a feeding frenzy," said David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network.

Menlow said underwriters were underestimating the recent psychological shift in the IPO market, which has changed to a buyers' from a sellers' market, and were not yet cutting the prices and valuations of new issues to reflect sentiment.

"Even good deals are pricing and trading right aronud their estimated ranges. And (weaker) ones, if they price at all, are cut by the number of shares or price or both. Some still trade lower," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.
"The market is very, very selective. There is money out there, it continues pouring into funds, but it is choosing new instruments -- namely blue chips," he said.

The issues that look best next week, Fitzgibbon reckons, are Poppe Tyson and Powerwave Technologies Inc, a maker of ultra-linear radio frequency power amplifiers used in the wireless communications market.
Alex Brown is the lead underwriter of Powerwave's offering of 1.8 million shares to price between $11 to $13 each.

Poppe Tyson Inc, part of Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt Inc, is an advertising agency specializing in the Internet and CD-ROMS. It has provided design services for the White House site on the World Wide Web, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc and Netscape Communications Corp.

But expectations for Poppe's opening debut have been dampening as its market debut gets pushed further into the future. It was originally expected to go public in the middle of November, but the deal was slightly delayed.
"That has a tendency to take some polish off the apple," Fitzgibbon said.

MoneyGram Payment Systems Inc, which has been in the pipeline since January, is also going public next week. Analysts have said the company has a sound business and good prospects for international growth.

Also at bat are Advanced Aerodynamics & Structures Inc, which makes propellor jet and jet aircraft, SkyMall, which offers products to airline passengers in-flight, Birman Managed Care, and Leading Edge Packaging Inc, which distributes packaging products used in the sale of luxury consumer products.
